theory.intro: An **annuity** is a sequence of equal, regular payments into an investment or loan. A period-by-period table tracks the interest earned on the opening balance and the regular payment added or subtracted at the end.
facts: Interest for each period is calculated on the **opening balance**: $I = \text{Opening Balance} \times r$.
For an investment annuity, the payment is **added** at the end: $\text{Closing} = \text{Opening} + I + \text{Payment}$.
For a reducing-balance loan, interest is added and the repayment is **subtracted**: $\text{Closing} = \text{Opening} + I - \text{Payment}$.
The closing balance of one period becomes the **opening balance** of the next period.
An investment recurrence relation is $V_{n} = V_{n-1}(1 + r) + D$, where $V_{0} = 0$.
A loan recurrence relation is $V_{n} = V_{n-1}(1 + r) - D$, where $V_{0}$ is the initial loan principal.
steps: Calculate interest on the opening balance for the period using $I = \text{Opening} \times r$.
Add the regular deposit (for savings) or subtract the repayment (for a loan).
Calculate the closing balance and carry it forward as the next period's opening balance.

foundation.question_text:
An investment account starts with $\$0$.
Deposits of $\$3000$ are made at the end of each year at $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Complete the table to find the balance at the end of Year $3$.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Year} & \text{Opening} & \text{Interest } (6\%) & \text{Deposit} & \text{Closing} \\ \hline 1 & \$0 & \$0 & \$3000 & \$3000 \\ 2 & \$3000 & \$180 & \$3000 & \$6180 \\ 3 & \$6180 & \text{---} & \$3000 & \text{---} \\ \hline \end{array}$

A personal loan of $\$4000$ incurs interest at $1\%$ per month ($12\%$ p.a.), with monthly repayments of $\$600$ made at the end of each month.
Complete the table to find the balance owing after $2$ months.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Month} & \text{Opening} & \text{Interest } (1\%) & \text{Repayment} & \text{Closing} \\ \hline 1 & \$4000 & \$40 & \$600 & \$3440 \\ 2 & \$3440 & \text{---} & \$600 & \text{---} \\ \hline \end{array}$

A savings annuity is modelled by the recurrence relation $V_{n} = V_{n-1} \times 1.05 + 800$, where $V_{0} = 0$.
Calculate the balance $V_{3}$ after $3$ payments.

A car loan is modelled by the recurrence relation $V_{n} = V_{n-1} \times 1.02 - 500$, where $V_{0} = 2000$.
Determine the balance $V_{2}$ after $2$ repayments.

An annuity investment table shows that after $4$ annual deposits of $\$1500$, the closing balance is $\$6820.65$.
Calculate the total interest earned over the $4$ years.

An account has $\$1000$ deposited at the end of each quarter at $2\%$ interest per quarter.
If the opening balance for Quarter $2$ is $\$1000$, find the interest earned in Quarter $2$ and the closing balance at the end of Quarter $2$.

development.question_text:
A loan of $\$10\,000$ charges interest at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly ($0.5\%$ per month), with monthly repayments of $\$800$.
Complete the table to find the closing balance at the end of Month $3$.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Month} & \text{Opening} & \text{Interest } (0.5\%) & \text{Repayment} & \text{Closing} \\ \hline 1 & \$10\,000 & \$50.00 & \$800 & \$9250.00 \\ 2 & \$9250.00 & \$46.25 & \$800 & \$8496.25 \\ 3 & \$8496.25 & \text{---} & \$800 & \text{---} \\ \hline \end{array}$

An investment annuity involves depositing $\$1200$ every $6$ months at $4\%$ p.a. compounded half-yearly ($r=0.02$).
Write the recurrence relation with $V_{0}=0$ and calculate the balance $V_{4}$ after $4$ half-years.

The table below shows the progress of a savings account over $3$ periods with equal deposits of $\$2000$ and fixed interest rate $r$.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Period} & \text{Opening} & \text{Interest} & \text{Deposit} & \text{Closing} \\ \hline 1 & \$0 & \$0 & \$2000 & \$2000 \\ 2 & \$2000 & \$100 & \$2000 & \$4100 \\ 3 & \$4100 & \text{---} & \$2000 & \text{---} \\ \hline \end{array}$
Find the periodic interest rate $r$ and the closing balance at the end of Period $3$.

A mortgage is modelled by $V_{n} = V_{n-1}(1.004) - 1500$, with $V_{0} = 180\,000$.
Calculate the balance owing $V_{3}$ after $3$ months, to the nearest cent.

For a $\$5000$ reducing-balance loan, repayments of $\$650$ are made at the end of each month for $4$ months, leaving a balance of $\$2542.80$.
Calculate the total interest charged over these $4$ months.

A borrower takes out a loan of $\$15\,000$ at $0.8\%$ monthly interest, making monthly repayments of $\$900$.
What is the opening balance, interest, and closing balance for Month $2$?

mastery.question_text:
A spreadsheet records an annuity investment where an initial lump sum of $\$5000$ is invested at the start of Month $1$, and further deposits of $\$400$ are added at the end of each month.
The monthly interest rate is $0.6\%$.
Find the closing balance at the end of Month $3$.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Month} & \text{Opening} & \text{Interest } (0.6\%) & \text{Deposit} & \text{Closing} \\ \hline 1 & \$5000.00 & \$30.00 & \$400 & \$5430.00 \\ 2 & \$5430.00 & \$32.58 & \$400 & \$5862.58 \\ 3 & \$5862.58 & \text{---} & \$400 & \text{---} \\ \hline \end{array}$

A debt of $\$8000$ is charged interest at $1.5\%$ per month, and repayments of $\$100$ per month are made.
Explain why the debt increases despite regular repayments, and evaluate the balance $V_{2}$ after $2$ months using $V_{n} = V_{n-1}(1.015) - 100$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Initial monthly interest} = 8000 \times 0.015 = \$120$
Since the repayment of $\$100$ is less than the $\$120$ interest, the debt grows.
$V_{1} = 8000(1.015) - 100 = 8120 - 100 = 8020$
$V_{2} = 8020(1.015) - 100 = 8140.30 - 100$
$=\$8040.30$

mastery.question_text:
Over $3$ periods, an annuity investment with opening balance $\$0$ has deposits of $\$1000$ per period at $4\%$ per period.
The interest earned in each period is $\$0$, $\$40$, and $\$81.60$ respectively.
Verify the closing balance after Period $3$ and find the total interest earned as a percentage of total deposits (to $2$ d.p.).
